title: The Humility of Christ
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The humility of Christ is His willing self-lowering in obedience, service, suffering, and death for the glory of the Father and the salvation of sinners. The Lord of glory came not to be served, but to serve.
summary: The humility of Christ is His willing self-lowering in obedience, service, suffering, and death for the glory of the Father and the salvation of sinners. The Lord of glory came not to be served, but to serve.
christFocus: Jesus reveals divine humility by taking the form of a servant and becoming obedient to death on a cross. His humility is not weakness but holy love in action.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The humility of Christ is seen most clearly in the incarnation and the cross. Though He is in the form of God, He humbled Himself, took the form of a servant, and became obedient unto death.

Jesus did not use His authority for selfish display. He welcomed the lowly, served His disciples, washed feet, bore shame, and moved toward sinners in grace and truth.

His humility does not deny His glory. The One who stooped is the One who is exalted. Christ’s lowliness reveals the beauty of His love and the character of His kingdom.

Believers are called to have the mind of Christ. Christian humility is not self-hatred; it is surrender to God, willingness to serve, and freedom from prideful self-exaltation.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Pride destroys discipleship, relationships, ministry, and worship. The humility of Christ confronts the desire to be noticed, served, praised, and obeyed by others.

This doctrine is also comfort for the lowly. Jesus does not despise humble places. He entered them, sanctified service, and showed that true greatness in His kingdom is shaped by love.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Follow the humility of Christ in daily life. Lay down pride, entitlement, bitterness, and the need to be seen. Serve others in love, receive correction, and remember that the Lord who humbled Himself for you is worthy of your whole life.
